questions.question: While driving, a driver should:

options.text: Not worry about what is happening on the sides of their vehicle.
Watch what is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
Not worry about what is happening behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch what is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must be aware of everything happening around your vehicle at all times. Look ahead and check both side mirrors regularly while driving.

questions.question: When inspecting the inside of a bus, a driver should check that:

options.text: Every seat is easy to remove.
There is no chipping paint.
All signaling devices work properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: All signaling devices work properly.
questions.explanation: When checking the inside of a bus, make sure everything is safe and working correctly. Check that all signaling devices, such as emergency buzzers, are in good working order.

questions.question: Before a trip, what should you look for under your vehicle as a warning sign?

options.text: A puddle of oil under the vehicle
Inflated tires
Lug nuts that look tight

questions.correctAnswerText: A puddle of oil under the vehicle
questions.explanation: Before your trip, look under the vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, coolant, grease, or fuel. Any fresh puddle of these fluids means there may be a safety problem.

questions.question: The danger of looking at your mirrors for too long is:

options.text: You will see potential hazards.
You will drive too far without seeing what is ahead on the road.
The mirrors may shake and move.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will drive too far without seeing what is ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: Looking at mirrors for too long is dangerous because you may drive a long distance without knowing what is ahead. You must be aware of your surroundings in all directions.

questions.question: An encroachment happens when:

options.text: A driver does not show up for their basic skills test.
A vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
A driver fails one part of the basic skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
questions.explanation: An encroachment during the basic skills test happens when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: Hydroplaning:

options.text: Rarely happens with large trucks.
Usually happens when vehicles go faster than 65 mph.
Can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is when your tires lose grip on the road and slide on water instead. You do not need a large amount of water on the road for this to happen.

questions.question: Steering wheel play of more than ____ can make steering hard.

options.text: 10 degrees
25 degrees
50 degrees

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 degrees
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should move no more than 10 degrees. This is about two inches of movement on a 20-inch wheel. Too much play makes steering difficult.

questions.question: On a curve, the posted speed limit:

options.text: Is safe for any vehicle.
Can still cause a vehicle to tip over.
Is the minimum legal speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can still cause a vehicle to tip over.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit on a curve may be safe for cars, but it can be too fast for larger vehicles like trucks. A truck driver going the posted limit on a curve could cause their vehicle to tip.

questions.question: How do ice cream trucks create hazards for other drivers?

options.text: Ice cream trucks must be kept cold.
Children often run toward ice cream trucks without looking for traffic.
Ice cream trucks leave water and ice on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children often run toward ice cream trucks without looking for traffic.
questions.explanation: Ice cream trucks create hazards because they attract children. Children often do not notice other vehicles when running toward or away from ice cream trucks.

questions.question: If brakes overheat while going downhill, they may:

options.text: Get sticky.
Stop working.
Squeak.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop working.
questions.explanation: Overusing brakes can make them overheat and stop working. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: When driving in hot weather:

options.text: Air pressure in tires will decrease.
Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.
Antifreeze is not needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.
questions.explanation: Hot air expands and increases tire pressure. Check your tire pressure in hot weather. Engine oil, water, and antifreeze all help prevent overheating. Antifreeze is important in both hot and cold weather.

questions.question: During a vehicle controls skills test, your vehicle's final position should be:

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact position the examiner described.
Within three feet of the position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position the examiner described.
questions.explanation: You must finish each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position the examiner described. Not following instructions exactly can result in failing the test.

questions.question: What is an example of required emergency equipment?

options.text: A spare electrical fuse.
A loud horn.
A battery-operated flashlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: A spare electrical fuse.
questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or three liquid flares, and a fire extinguisher.

questions.question: When passengers have carry-on baggage, it is best to:

options.text: Place items in front of the rear exit door.
Leave items near the front door.
Secure items so all exits are easily accessible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure items so all exits are easily accessible.
questions.explanation: Baggage cannot block doorways or aisles. It must be secured to prevent damage, allow the driver to move freely, let riders exit easily in an emergency, and protect riders from injury.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the roadway:

options.text: Is expected to be on the roadway.
Is usually empty and safe.
Could contain a heavy object that damages vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Could contain a heavy object that damages vehicles.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road can be dangerous. A cardboard box might look harmless but could contain something hard or heavy that damages your vehicle.

questions.question: When placing warning triangles on the road:

options.text: Hold triangles between you and oncoming traffic.
Hide triangles behind your back until you place them.
Hold triangles as low as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold triangles between you and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: For your safety, carry warning triangles between your body and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When traction is poor, accelerate slowly to:

options.text: Follow safe driving rules.
Keep from losing control of the vehicle.
Stay behind the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep from losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly on slippery roads. Too much power on slippery surfaces causes you to lose control.

questions.question: Confused drivers:

options.text: Often change direction suddenly.
Often turn on emergency flashers to warn others.
Often look like other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often change direction suddenly.
questions.explanation: Confused drivers are dangerous because they may change directions suddenly. Signs of confusion include hesitant driving or unexpected stops. Out-of-state plates or luggage may indicate the driver is unfamiliar with the area.

questions.question: Which of the following is not required safety equipment?

options.text: A fire extinguisher
A liquid burning flare
An axe

questions.correctAnswerText: An axe
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have proper emergency equipment including spare fuses, reflective triangles or liquid flares, and a fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Why should part of your vehicle be visible in a side mirror?

options.text: It limits the view behind the trailer.
It gives you a point of reference.
It lets you see stickers on the trailer side.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you a point of reference.
questions.explanation: Adjust side mirrors to show part of your vehicle. This helps you judge the location of nearby objects.
